name: Borong village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Family-run rooms scattered across upper Borong, about 5 km beyond Ralang Monastery at roughly 1,770 m. Simple, clean, home-cooked food, and a front-row view of Kangchenjunga, Pandim and Narsing on clear mornings. The base for the Borong hot spring and the Maenam ridge walk.
body: Borong is a farming village spread down the slope below Maenam hill, about 17 km from Ravangla by road. A handful of households take guests in spare rooms or small cottages built beside the family house. Expect a double or triple room with an attached bathroom, hot water by geyser or bucket, and meals eaten with the family: rice, dal, a seasonal green such as squash shoots or nettle, and pickle made from the hosts' own chillies.

We book Borong for travellers who want quiet more than amenities. The road ends close by, there is little traffic after dark, and the birding along the cardamom terraces is good in spring. The Borong tsachu (hot spring) on the Rangeet is a steep walk below the village and is used most in December to February. Mobile signal is patchy; tell family at home you may be offline for a night.
why: Kangchenjunga and Pandim views from most rooms on clear days
Walk down to the Borong hot spring and back from your door
Home-cooked Sikkimese meals with the host family

faqs.q: How do we get to Borong homestays?
faqs.a: Most guests come by private car from Ravangla, about 17 km and 45 minutes via Ralang. Shared jeeps run between Ravangla and Borong a few times a day, mostly in the morning, but timings shift, so ask your host. From Gangtok it is roughly 85 km and 4 hours. Check current status before you travel, as the last stretch can be rough after heavy rain.

faqs.q: What does a Borong homestay cost?
faqs.a: Plan on about ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night including dinner and breakfast, sometimes lunch too. Prices depend on the room (attached bathroom, view) and the season. Bring cash: few homes take cards, and the nearest ATMs are in Ravangla. These are indicative figures, so confirm the rate and what meals are included when you book.

faqs.q: Is Borong good in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, if you pack warm. December to February brings the clearest mountain views and is the season when local families walk down to the hot spring to bathe. Nights drop close to freezing, and rooms are not centrally heated, so carry thermals and ask for an extra quilt. Snow is rare at village level but possible on Maenam above.

name: Kewzing village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,500–2,500 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: A Bhutia village on the Ravangla–Legship road that started a community homestay programme in 2003. A village tourism committee shares guests between participating families. Rooms are in family homes among cardamom, maize and vegetable plots, a short drive from the Bon monastery.
body: Kewzing sits at roughly 1,500–1,600 m, about 10 km below Ravangla towards Legship. Down To Earth reported that the villagers formed an elected body, the Kewzing Tourism Development Committee, to run the programme and spread income fairly between host families rather than letting one or two homes take every guest. That model is why we like sending people here: your money stays in the village.

Hosts are mostly Bhutia Buddhist families who still farm. Guests can join in with whatever the season brings: drying cardamom in autumn, planting in spring, making butter tea or churpi. Rooms are simple and clean, usually with attached bathrooms, and meals are home-cooked. Ask your host to walk you to Kewzing's Bon monastery, one of the very few in India.
why: A community-run homestay programme that spreads income across families
Farm days in cardamom and vegetable plots
Short walk or drive to the Bon monastery at Kewzing

faqs.q: How is a Kewzing homestay booked?
faqs.a: Bookings are usually handled through the village tourism committee or directly with a host family, and we can arrange it as part of a trip. The committee decides which family hosts you so that guests are shared out. Tell us about food needs, children or mobility issues in advance so the right home can be matched. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is there to do in Kewzing?
faqs.a: Walk the village paths, visit the Bon monastery founded in 1974, help with farm work, and take a day trip to Ravangla's Buddha Park and Ralang Monastery, each within about 30 minutes by car. Birders do well on the forest edges early in the morning. Evenings are quiet, often spent around the kitchen fire with the family.

faqs.q: Is Kewzing suitable for children and seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. Kewzing is lower and milder than Ravangla, and the main road runs right through the village, so you are never far from a car. Some homes have steps down to the rooms, so mention knee or mobility issues when booking. Food is simple and not very spicy unless you ask for chilli.

name: Yangang village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: A small group of family homestays in Yangang, a Lepcha, Bhutia and Nepali village below Maenam hill on the Ravangla side. Expect simple rooms, home food and early starts for the Bhaleydhunga and Maenam ridge. Useful for travellers who want a working village rather than a resort town.
body: Yangang lies at about 1,500 m on the eastern flank of the Maenam ridge, roughly 30–40 minutes by car from Ravangla. It is a mixed village of Lepcha, Bhutia and Nepali families, with a Lepcha monastery, a Gurung monastery and fields of maize, ginger and cardamom. The state has run training for rural homestays here under a central MSME programme, and several homes now take guests.

A Yangang homestay suits walkers and people curious about village life. Hosts can point you to Neya Khola falls, the village monasteries and the forest trail towards Bhaleydhunga, the rock on Maenam's south face. Facilities are basic but clean; hot water may come by bucket. We match guests to homes we know and brief hosts on dietary needs beforehand.
why: Mixed Lepcha, Bhutia and Nepali village life
Close to the Maenam and Bhaleydhunga forest walks
Low prices, home food, almost no traffic

faqs.q: Where exactly is Yangang?
faqs.a: Yangang is in Namchi district (South Sikkim), below Maenam hill and north-east of Ravangla. By car it is about 30–40 minutes from Ravangla and around 3 hours from Gangtok. Local shared jeeps link Yangang with Ravangla and Singtam, mostly in the morning and early afternoon. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can we walk to Bhaleydhunga from Yangang?
faqs.a: The Maenam ridge and the Bhaleydhunga rock are above Yangang and are usually approached on a long forest day walk with a local guide. It is steep, can be muddy and is best done October to April. A ropeway and skywalk have been proposed for Bhaleydhunga but are not open; do not plan around them.

faqs.q: Do Yangang homestays have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: Some homes have Wi-Fi or decent 4G, many do not, and power cuts happen in storms. Treat a night here as offline time and download maps beforehand. Carry a torch and a power bank. If you need to work online, stay in Ravangla and visit Yangang as a day trip instead.

name: Mt. Narsing Village Resort
summary: A long-running cottage resort on the Ravangla–Pelling road, a few kilometres from Ravangla town. Two wings at different prices, lawns and gardens, an indoor fireplace in the dining room, and a wide view over the Rangeet valley to Narsing and Kabru.
body: Mt. Narsing Village Resort has been one of Ravangla's familiar addresses for years. It sits off the highway towards Legship and Pelling, among village fields rather than in the market, so evenings are quiet. The roadside wing is simpler and cheaper; the annexe has cottages and better rooms with mountain views. The restaurant serves Sikkimese, Indian, Chinese and continental dishes.

We use it for value-tier trips where guests want a garden and a view without resort prices. It is a short drive to Buddha Park and Ralang Monastery and an easy start for the Maenam walk. Rooms are not luxurious, and standards vary between wings, so ask for the annexe if the view matters. Breakfast is usually included in the rate.
why: Garden cottages with views of Narsing and Kabru
Quiet location away from Ravangla market
Easy drive to Buddha Park, Ralang and Borong

faqs.q: How far is Mt. Narsing Village Resort from Buddha Park?
faqs.a: Roughly 15 minutes by car. The resort is a few kilometres from Ravangla on the road towards Legship and Pelling, and Buddha Park is just above Ravangla town. Ralang Monastery is around 20–25 minutes away. A taxi from the resort to Ravangla market and back costs about ₹300–500 if you do not have your own car.

faqs.q: Which wing should we choose?
faqs.a: The annexe wing with cottages has the better rooms and the mountain view, and costs more. The roadside wing is cheaper and fine for one night, but simpler. If you are visiting in October–November or March–April for the views, the annexe is worth the extra. Confirm the wing in writing when you book.

faqs.q: Is it warm enough in winter?
faqs.a: Ravangla is around 2,000 m and drops near freezing on December–February nights. The dining room has a fireplace, and rooms have heaters on request, sometimes for a charge. Pack thermals, a warm hat and socks for evenings. Clear winter mornings bring the best views of Narsing and Kabru.

name: Cherry Resort, Temi
image_query: Cherry Resort Temi Tea Garden Sikkim
summary: A mid-range resort inside the Temi tea estate, on land owned by the Sikkim Tourism Development Corporation and run privately. Rooms look over tea bushes towards the Teesta gorge and Kangchenjunga. Walk out of the door into the estate at dawn.
body: Cherry Resort began life as the state-run Yatri Niwas at Temi and was later leased out to a private operator, which is why it is the only proper resort right inside the estate. Almost every room faces tea: rows of bushes running down the hill, cherry trees along the factory road, and on clear days the Kangchenjunga range across the valley. The restaurant serves Indian and Sikkimese food and, of course, Temi tea.

We use Cherry Resort for families and couples who want to wake up in the garden and walk the estate before the day's visitors arrive from Namchi and Ravangla. Rooms are comfortable rather than plush. Book early for November, when the cherry blossom is out and the state's Cherry Tea Festival fills the area.
why: Rooms inside the Temi tea estate with valley views
Early-morning walks on estate paths before day visitors
Good base in cherry-blossom season (November)

faqs.q: Is Cherry Resort actually inside Temi Tea Garden?
faqs.a: Yes. The resort stands within the estate on land owned by the Sikkim Tourism Development Corporation, and is now run by a private lessee. You can walk straight onto the estate paths and down towards the factory. The estate itself is run by the state government, so follow plucking-area rules and ask before entering the factory.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay at Cherry Resort?
faqs.a: October to early December and March to May. November brings cherry blossom along the estate road and the state's Cherry Tea Festival, held most years since 2018. Spring is good for first-flush plucking. June to August is wet and views are often lost in cloud, though the bushes are at their greenest.

faqs.q: How do we reach Cherry Resort from Gangtok?
faqs.a: By private car it is roughly 50–55 km and 2.5–3 hours via Singtam and Tarku. From Ravangla it is under an hour, and from Namchi about 1.5 hours. There is no reliable direct shared jeep to the resort gate, so most guests come by car. Check current status before you travel during the monsoon.

name: Bon Farmhouse
summary: A family-run farmstay at Kewzing, set among a few acres of tea, cardamom and vegetable fields below Ravangla. Responsible-travel listings have featured it for years. Simple, characterful rooms, farm food and an easy walk to Kewzing's Bon monastery.
body: Bon Farmhouse takes its name from Kewzing's Bon monastery nearby, and is run by a local family on their own farm. The setting is a working plot of tea bushes, cardamom under shade trees and kitchen gardens, with Narsing and Kabru visible on clear days. Rooms are in the family property and cottages built around it, with wooden interiors and attached bathrooms.

It suits travellers who want more comfort than a village homestay but still want to eat what the farm grows. Expect organic vegetables, local cheese and pickles, and help with picking or sorting if you ask. It is about 20 minutes from Ravangla's Buddha Park and a good overnight between Pelling and Namchi.
why: Farm setting with tea, cardamom and kitchen gardens
More comfort than a homestay, same home food
Walk to the Bon monastery; 20 minutes to Buddha Park

faqs.q: Is Bon Farmhouse a homestay or a hotel?
faqs.a: In between. It is family-run on a working farm, with meals cooked at home, but rooms are more private and better finished than a typical village homestay. Think of it as a farmstay. Book with meals included, as there are few eating options nearby in the evening.

faqs.q: How far is Bon Farmhouse from Pelling?
faqs.a: Kewzing is on the Ravangla–Legship road. Pelling is roughly 40 km and about 2 hours by car via Legship and Gyalshing. Ravangla is about 20 minutes uphill. That makes it a sensible overnight on a west-to-south loop: Pelling, Kewzing, then Ravangla or Namchi.

faqs.q: What can we do on the farm?
faqs.a: Depending on the season you can help pick vegetables, watch cardamom being dried (September to November), walk the fields and village paths, and visit the Bon monastery. Birdwatching is good early in the morning. Ask the family the evening before so someone can show you around.

name: Seven Hill Resort
summary: A cottage resort on about six acres of sloping, landscaped ground at Phalidara above Namchi. Traditionally designed cottages with balconies face Samdruptse, Solophok's Char Dham and, on clear days, Kangchenjunga, with Darjeeling's ridge in the distance.
body: Seven Hill Resort is out of the town centre, reached by a winding drive through trees, which keeps it quiet. Cottages are spread across the slope rather than stacked in a block, so most have their own balcony and view. From the terrace you can pick out the Guru Rinpoche statue at Samdruptse, the Rock Garden, the helipad and the Shiva statue on Solophok.

We place comfort-tier guests here when they want space and a view rather than a lift and a lobby. It works well for families: lawns, room to walk, and a short drive to all of Namchi's sights. Food is multi-cuisine. Ask for a cottage facing north for the mountain and west for the sunset.
why: Spread-out cottages with private balconies
Views of Samdruptse, Char Dham and Kangchenjunga
Quiet location a short drive from Namchi's sights

faqs.q: How far is Seven Hill Resort from Char Dham?
faqs.a: Around 15–20 minutes by car. The resort is at Phalidara above Namchi; Char Dham on Solophok hill is about 5 km from town on the other side, and Samdruptse is a similar distance. With a car you can do both in one morning and be back for lunch.

faqs.q: Is the resort suitable for elderly travellers?
faqs.a: Mostly yes. Cottages are on a slope, so some involve steps; ask for one close to the dining area when you book. Namchi is around 1,500 m, mild and easy on the body compared with North Sikkim, and the town has a district hospital. Bring a light jacket even in summer evenings.

faqs.q: Does Seven Hill Resort have mountain views?
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days. Kangchenjunga shows best from October to early December and on winter mornings. In the monsoon (June to September) clouds usually hide the peaks, though the valley views towards Samdruptse and Solophok remain. Sunsets over the Darjeeling ridge are a regular evening show.

name: The Barfung Retreat
summary: A small cottage retreat in Barfung village just outside Ravangla, above the village primary school. Wood-panelled rooms in three cottages, breakfast included, and walking paths straight from the gate. Good for couples and families who want Ravangla without the market noise.
body: Barfung is a Bhutia village on the slope near Ravangla, and the retreat is built to feel like part of it: three cottages with wooden floors and panelled walls, rooms from standard deluxe up to suites, tea and coffee makers, desks and blackout curtains. It is small enough that staff learn your name by the second morning.

We use it for comfort-tier trips around Buddha Park, Ralang and Temi. The location gives you a village walk before breakfast and a short drive into Ravangla for the monastery circuit. The restaurant is multi-cuisine; ask for Sikkimese dishes a day ahead. Families with young children like the open space and quiet.
why: Small, quiet cottage retreat in a Bhutia village
Wood-panelled rooms with blackout curtains for cold nights
Village walks from the gate; short drive to Buddha Park

faqs.q: Where is The Barfung Retreat?
faqs.a: In Barfung village on the outskirts of Ravangla, above the Barfung primary school. It is a few minutes by car from Ravangla market and about 15 minutes from Buddha Park. If you arrive by shared jeep from Gangtok or Namchi, a local taxi from Ravangla stand will drop you for around ₹200–300.

faqs.q: Is breakfast included at The Barfung Retreat?
faqs.a: Breakfast is normally included in room rates, and lunch and dinner are available at the restaurant. We usually book half board (breakfast and dinner) because Barfung has few other places to eat after dark. Confirm the meal plan when you book, as packages vary by season.

faqs.q: Is it good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes, if you prefer quiet to nightlife. Ask for a suite or a room in the cottage furthest from the reception. Pair it with a night at Temi tea garden and a morning at Buddha Park. October–November and March–April bring the clearest weather and mild days.

name: Sobralia Hotels Casino Resort & Spa
summary: Namchi's largest upmarket hotel, formerly Summit Sobralia Resort & Spa, on the road up to Char Dham. A five-storey building with valley and Kangchenjunga views from the rooms, a spa, gym, multi-cuisine restaurant and a small casino floor.
body: Sobralia is the most complete hotel in South Sikkim: lift, suites, spa, gym, meditation room and a restaurant that can handle a large family or group. It sits on the road from Namchi to Siddhesvara Dham (Char Dham), so you can be at the Shiva statue before the coach parties. Upper floors look across the Rangeet valley to the Kangchenjunga range.

We use it for premium and comfort-plus trips where guests want hotel services rather than a cottage resort. Note that South Sikkim has no five-star palaces; Sobralia is the top of the local market, not a Taj. The casino area is small. Ask for a high floor facing north for the mountain view.
why: Namchi's most complete hotel: lift, spa, gym, suites
Upper floors look across the Rangeet valley to Kangchenjunga
On the road to Char Dham for an early start

faqs.q: Is Sobralia the same as Summit Sobralia?
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel was earlier marketed as Summit Sobralia Resort & Spa and now trades as Sobralia Hotels Casino Resort & Spa. Some booking sites still show the old name. It is the same building on the road between Namchi town and Siddhesvara Dham (Char Dham).

faqs.q: Does Sobralia have a lift and easy access?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a multi-storey hotel with a lift, which makes it one of the better choices in Namchi for seniors or anyone who finds stairs hard. The rest of Namchi's sights involve some walking: Char Dham has ramps and steps, Samdruptse has a long flight of steps up to the statue.

faqs.q: How far is Sobralia from Samdruptse?
faqs.a: About 20–25 minutes by car, through Namchi town and up the Samdruptse road past the Rock Garden. Char Dham is closer, roughly 10 minutes. A full Namchi sightseeing circuit from the hotel (Char Dham, Samdruptse, Rock Garden, Ngadak monastery) takes 4–5 hours with a car.

name: The Temi Bungalow (Eco Adventure Resorts)
price_band: ≈ ₹12,000–20,000 a room a night with meals (indicative)
summary: The restored Bada Bungalow inside the state-owned Temi tea estate, now run by Eco Adventure Resorts with newer cottages around it. Old missionary-era architecture, a verandah over the tea, indoor dining and tea tastings. The most characterful high-end stay in South Sikkim.
body: The Bada Bungalow is one of the old mission buildings that predate the tea estate, which the Chogyal's government founded in 1969. It was badly damaged in the 2011 Sikkim earthquake and later restored, keeping its colonial-era lines, verandah and fireplaces. Newer cottages built in a matching style stand around it. The estate is run by the Sikkim government; the bungalow is managed by Eco Adventure Resorts.

We book it for premium trips and special occasions: tea tastings, walks with estate staff, slow breakfasts on the verandah with Kangchenjunga across the valley. Rates are high by local standards and usually include meals. Rooms in the old bungalow have the most atmosphere; cottages have more space and privacy.
why: Restored mission-era bungalow inside the Temi estate
Tea tastings and estate walks arranged on site
Verandah and fireplaces, with Kangchenjunga across the valley

faqs.q: How old is the Temi Bungalow?
faqs.a: The Bada Bungalow is one of the missionary-era buildings on the Temi slope, put up long before the tea estate was founded in 1969. Published accounts date it to the late 1800s; we treat the exact year as uncertain. It was damaged in the 2011 earthquake and restored before reopening as a heritage stay.

faqs.q: Who runs the Temi Bungalow?
faqs.a: The tea estate belongs to the Government of Sikkim. The bungalow and its cottages are managed by Eco Adventure Resorts, a private hospitality operator. That is why the stay feels more like a small boutique hotel than a government guest house, with prices to match.

faqs.q: Is the Temi Bungalow worth the price?
faqs.a: If you value atmosphere, quiet and tea, yes. You get the estate largely to yourself in the early morning, meals included and a building with real history. If you only want a clean room near Temi, Cherry Resort costs roughly a third as much. We often split a trip: one night here, the rest at value hotels.
